simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sinas: sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm — to allow, let, permit (2nd sg. pres. subj.)
sine: sine (prep. + abl.) — without · also sinō, -ere, sīvī, situm, to allow, let (sg. imper.: sine palmula)
sint: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
siquando: sīquandō (sī quandō) — if ever, if at any time (adv./conj.)
sit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
solebant: soleō, -ēre, solitus sum — to be accustomed, be wont (3rd pl. impf.)
stabat: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd sg. impf.)
steterat: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3 sg. pluperf.)
stirpe: stirps, stirpis (f.) — stock, root, lineage (abl. sg.)
stirpem: stirps, stirpis (f.) — stock, root, stem; lineage, race (acc. sg.)
struis: struō, -ere, strūxī, strūctum — to build, contrive, plan (2nd sg. pres.)
stygii: Stygius, -a, -um — of the Styx, Stygian, infernal (m. nom. pl.) · also m. gen. sg.
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sublimes: sublīmis, -e — raised aloft, high up, lofty (m./f. nom./acc. pl.)
subridens: subrīdeō, subrīdēre, subrīsī — to smile (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
succurrere: succurrō, -ere, -currī, -cursum — to run to help, aid (+ dat.) (pres. inf.)
superis: superus, -a, -um — upper, above; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
superstitio: superstitiō, -ōnis (f.) — superstition, awe of the gods (nom. sg.)
supra: suprā (adv., prep. + acc.) — above, over, on top
supremum: suprēmus, -a, -um — last, final, uttermost (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
surget: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise, spring up (3rd sg. fut.)
tacitam: tacitus, -a, -um — silent, still, unspeaking (f. acc. sg.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tantos: tantus, -a, -um — so great, so much (m. acc. pl.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem) · also n. acc. sg. adj. (tantum rōbur)
tantus: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. sg.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
teloque: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear (abl. sg.) + -que, and
telumque: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, weapon (nom./acc. sg.) + -que, and
temptare: temptō (tentō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to try, probe, test, attempt (pres. inf.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenebunt: teneō, -ēre, -uī, tentum — to hold, keep, reach and hold (3rd pl. fut.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
tenetur: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, grip, keep (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
territus: terreō, -ēre, terruī, territum — to frighten, terrify (perf. part., m. nom. sg.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
teucrosque: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, the Trojans (acc. pl.) + -que, and
tolli: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift up, carry off, take away (pres. pass. inf.)
tonat: tonō, -āre, -uī — to thunder, roar (3rd sg. pres.)
totidemque: totidem (indecl.) — just as many, the same number + -que 'and'
trementis: tremō, -ere, tremuī — to tremble, quiver (pres. part., f. acc. pl., = -ēs; also m./f./n. gen. sg.)
trepidique: trepidus, -a, -um — anxious, alarmed, trembling (m. nom. pl., with Latīnī) + -que 'and'
tristes: tristis, -e — sad, sorrowful, gloomy (f./m. nom. pl.)
troas: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (acc. pl., Greek form Trōas)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
troianos: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (m. acc. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuentem: tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum (dep.) — to look at, gaze on (pres. part., m. acc. sg.; torva tuentem)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuorum: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.); tuōrum, of your people (m. gen. pl.)
tuos: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m. acc. pl.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnum: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (acc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
ullis: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. abl. pl.) · also m./n. dat. pl. (caelestibus ūllīs)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
uno: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (m./n. abl. sg.)
urget: urgeō, -ēre, ursī — to press, push hard, urge on, bear down on (3rd sg. pres.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
utque: ut (conj.) — that, so that, as, when (+ -que 'and')
valuit: valeō, -ēre, valuī — to be strong, be able, prevail (3rd sg. perf.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
veluti: velut, velutī (adv.) — just as, as when
venerabile: venerābilis, -e — worthy of reverence, venerable (n. acc. sg.; venerābile dōnum)
ventum: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (perf. pass. part., n. sg., in impersonal ventum est, they came) · also ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (acc. sg.: in ventum, 'into the wind')
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertere: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, change, drive (pres. inf.) · also 3rd pl. perf. = vertērunt (vōcem vertere procellae)
verum: vērum (conj.) — but, but yet (adverbial n. acc. sg. of vērus) · also vērus, -a, -um — true, real (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
vetus: vetus, -eris — old, ancient, long-standing (n. acc. sg.; also m./f./n. nom. sg., m./f. acc. sg.)
victis: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — to conquer (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. pl.) · also dat. pl. (ūna salūs victīs)
videbis: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. fut.)
videres: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. impf. subj.)
vim: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (acc. sg.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres.: Vīs … vidēre?)
vita: vīta, -ae (f.) — life, living; the breath of life (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
vocans: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, invoke, summon (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
vocari: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon, name (pres. pass. inf.)
vocavit: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. perf.)
vocem: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (acc. sg.)
voluntas: voluntās, -ātis (f.) — will, wish, purpose, resolve (nom. sg.)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
